description:
FILED s532 (Fable 5.1, 2026-11-02) from the round board run on MAIN-READY-63 b31345ca (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s532/review/board-main63.rows.tsv): NEW rows Template-Toolkit compile2.t #1 #2 (unnamed) + *PLAN* "ran 5 of 9", compile5.t *PLAN* "ran 3 of 3, rc 2" + rows 1-3 "cached foo / bar / blam"; s531a had already noted that compile2.t / compile5.t depend on compile1.t / compile4.t running FIRST (its rows were measured by one-file runs in order on the combined tree, docs/session-log.md "Rebases and the register").  MECHANISM: tools/cpan-scoreboard.pl builds @work from every dist's sorted t/ listing and spawns `shift @queue` onto $jobs workers (lines ~277-414): compile2.t starts while compile1.t is still writing t/test/src/*.ttc (and compile5.t before compile4.t) -- perl's `make test` runs a dist's files in sequence, so the dist relies on it.  The blessed rows for compile2/compile5 are therefore ORDER-DEPENDENT in a whole-board run and the board's --diff cannot tell an order artifact from a regression.  FIX SHAPE (tools layer, task #1502's instrument): a per-dist flag in baselines/cpan-board-dists.tsv (`--serial`: the dist's files run one at a time in sorted order on ONE worker while other dists fill the other workers) -- or a dependency column `after=FILE` per file in baselines/cpan-board-timeouts.tsv's sibling registry; measure the board's wall time BEFORE -> AFTER (TT has 121 files, most under 5 s).  Until then: the TT compile rows are verified by one-file runs in order (compile1..5 in ONE run-dist-t.pl invocation or sequentially), never from a whole-board run; the s532 round's compile2/compile5 NEW rows are NOT blessed (artifact).  Layer: tools.  Queued: s532b (tools member).

=== DONE (s532b) ===
FIXED (tools layer): baselines/cpan-board-dists.tsv's flags column takes `--serial` (several flags space-separated now); tools/cpan-board.sh passes `--dist-serial` before the dist; tools/cpan-scoreboard.pl runs a serial dist's files one at a time in sorted order (next_ready skips a busy serial dist's items, so the other workers take other dists) and puts the serial chain FIRST in the queue (at the end it would run alone).  Template-Toolkit is flagged.  tools/t/cpan-scoreboard.t row: a two-file dist whose b.t reads a.t's marker -- PASS with --dist-serial on two workers, FAIL without (checked).  Wall: see the session-log section (TT alone serial vs parallel).


=== s532b MEASURED (2026-11-06, scratch/s532b/tt-board.log) ===
The whole-dist `--serial` was MEASURED too slow and dropped: 51 of 121 TT files in 22 min on one worker (scratch/s532b/tt-board-wholedist-killed.log) -- the chain would have been the board's critical path.  So the flag takes a REGEX (`--serial=REGEX`: only the matching t-names form the chain, started first) and TT is `--serial=^compile`.
TT ALONE, 4 workers, a loaded box: `--serial=^compile` wall 1271 s, --diff 0 NEW; plain parallel wall 941 s, --diff 7 NEW = compile2.t #0 #2, compile3.t #5, compile5.t #0 #1 #2 #3 (the order race).  On the whole board the other dists fill the other workers beside the chain.  Both runs: 7 TT rows FIXED vs the blessed file (service.t 7 23, stop.t 16 17, string.t 79 81 83) -- not attributed yet; a base one-file run decides before they leave the baseline.
subject: The CPAN board runs a dist's t-files from one sorted queue on 4-8 workers, so a file that depends on an EARLIER file's side effect races it: Template-Toolkit compile2.t / compile5.t read the .ttc cache compile1.t / compile4.t write, and read FAIL / extra NEW rows in a whole-board run while a one-file run in order passes -- the board needs a per-dist serial (or ordered-dependency) rule
